name: template-library-loader
body: Template library loader: resolves the deck's library layers from the deck config — the external library at the `templates:` path when set (relative to the deck root, or absolute) and the deck-root `templates/` directory when it exists — where a configured path is authoritative for the external layer (the local `templates/` is a second layer, never a fallback), and neither layer resolving is a templates error (templates-dir-required); then reads each layer via an fs.FS rooted at it, validates it fail-fast in the templates-dir-validation order (each layer's library.yaml; that layer's structure — the library structure is library.yaml, slides/, sections/, themes/, media/, and any other top-level entry (`.git/`, README, `AGENTS_KALIDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, an editor lockfile, …) is inert (library-guide-layout), outside the parsed, validated, rendered, listed and served set; per template in `slides/<name>/` and `sections/<name>/`: required files, `template.yaml` well-formed (a `usage:` key is a templates error, domain.constraint.template-defects-build-time), layout parses as standard html/template with the registry's function map (the helpers `media`, `section`, `dict`, `list`, `child`, `children`), errors file:line-qualified; the registry's build checks then reject reference cycles with the chain in the error — a reference is a declared `sections:` acceptance, a `section` helper call in a layout, or a `child` constructor's target (section-helper-load-checks, child-constructor) —, reject any composition chain deeper than six heading levels, check each `section` helper call (the target is a defined section-usage template, literal `dict` keys are declared fields, required fields are present or defaulted, each literal child argument's template is accepted by the target's declared sections and its fields/body/nested children validate, the literal child set satisfies each declaration's min/max), and validate each `example.md` — including a container template's example with nested instances — recursively, executing each template's example layout against the merged layout namespace built from every library layout text with the template's own layer function map, so `{{ template "<name>" . }}` composition resolves per layer while `media` binds to the template's own layer (example-layout-composition); themes have theme.css; references — in a theme's `theme.css` and every stylesheet it imports within that layer (the same theme dir, another theme dir, or `media/`; imports followed, bounded and cycle-safe across the whole import graph, cycles detected): a relative `url()`/`@import` resolves from the importing file's own location and must stay inside that file's own tree (its theme directory, or `media/` for a stylesheet imported through `media:`; cross-tree reach is only through `media:` / `theme:<name>/`), a `url()`/`@import` with the reserved `media:` prefix resolves to an existing file under that layer's `media/` (relative and staying within `media/`), and a `url()`/`@import` with the reserved `theme:<name>/` prefix resolves to an existing file inside that layer's theme directory (an unknown `<name>` is an error); a missing file, an absolute path, a `..` leaving its own tree, or any other scheme is file:line-qualified to the offending CSS; plus layout src/href inside that template's layer and every layout `media "path"` argument relative and staying within that layer's `media/`, naming an existing file, layout violations file:line-qualified to the layout), merges the layers into one library and rejects any slide, section, theme or media name carried by both (library-layer-uniqueness), requires the external layer to be self-contained (its templates and themes reference only the external library, so it validates on its own; library-layer-references) while a local template's `section` helper call resolves against the merged set, the merged library's single-root convenience fields — `Meta`, `Root`, `RootPath`, `Media` and `HasMedia` — describe the primary layer: the deck-root local `templates/` layer of a two-layer deck, or the sole layer of a single-root library, so in a two-layer deck a media root reachable under the unprefixed `/assets/templates/media/` URL comes from the local layer and never the external one, while each contributing layer's own metadata, root, media, themes and `Role` (`sole`, `external` or `local`) stay on that layer's `Layers` entry, ordered external first then local when both contribute, assigns each template its kind from its directory, parses each `template.yaml` into the template schema model and registers templates (template-registry) and themes (theme-registry); returns the first templates error path-qualified with the offending file's on-disk path in its OS's native canonical form (native-display-paths). Single source for start, templates, gallery and reload. A running session resolves the startup-pinned `templates:` value for the external layer; a changed value keeps the pinned root and the reload pipeline surfaces the restart-required error (see solution.component.http-server, template-retarget-requires-restart, global.constraint.never-serve-broken-deck).
